name: acute abdomen overview
title: Abdominal pain: first decide whether it is an acute surgical abdomen, then sort it into peritonitis (generalized or focal), perforation or ischemic bowel, with obstruction and bleeding sent to their own charts; a non-surgical abdomen is worked through system by system; each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment in order

root.title: Abdominal pain: is this an ACUTE (SURGICAL) ABDOMEN?
lines: history: timing, severity, location, what makes it worse, gynecologic, sexual, drugs, travel
exam: vitals · inspect, auscultate, percuss, palpate · pelvic exam · rectal exam · heart and lungs

groups.title: YES: perforation, ischemia, obstruction or bleeding
lines: OBSTRUCTION: BOWEL OBSTRUCTION chart · BLEEDING: GI bleeding notes

head: h
Peritonitis
inflamed peritoneum: an EMERGENCY (sepsis)
tx: 1 · IV fluids, nothing by mouth, broad-spectrum antibiotics
GENERALIZED (> 1 quadrant) → prepare for the operating room
FOCAL (1 quadrant) → may be managed without surgery

head: h
Ischemic bowel
superior mesenteric artery most often
EMBOLIC (atrial fibrillation, previous heart attack) > thrombotic
pres: • pain OUT OF PROPORTION to the exam
• fever, fast heart rate, looks unwell
tx: 1 · Fluids, nothing by mouth, antibiotics → RESECTION
• LARGE: low flow, medical treatment usually works

head: h
Everything else
most common system first
inv: abdominal or chest X-ray, ultrasound, CT abdomen/pelvis
